info.name: SwiftGoma
info.description:
Complete API collection for the SwiftGoma backend (`server/`) — a Node.js + Express + Prisma/PostgreSQL API powering the SwiftGoma marketplace's four apps (Buyer, Seller, Rider/Delivery, Admin Dashboard).

**Base URL & versioning.** Every request is built from `{{baseUrl}}{{apiVersion}}/...`. Defaults: `baseUrl = http://localhost:4000`, `apiVersion = /api/v1`, matching the server's default port (`PORT` env, default 4000) and its `app.use("/api/v1/...", ...)` route mounts. Update `baseUrl` in the collection variables to point at a deployed environment.

**Response envelope.** Every endpoint returns `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors return `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with a matching HTTP status (400 BAD_REQUEST, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, 403 FORBIDDEN, 404 NOT_FOUND, 409 CONFLICT, 422 VALIDATION_ERROR, 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS/IP_BLOCKED, 500 INTERNAL_ERROR).

**Authentication.** The collection's default auth is Bearer (`Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`), applied to every request except those explicitly marked "No Auth" (public endpoints and provider webhook callbacks, which use their own signature-verification scheme instead — see the Payments webhook folders). Run a login request first (Authentication folder) — its test script stores `accessToken`/`refreshToken`/`userId` into the collection variables automatically. The server also supports httpOnly-cookie sessions for browser clients (send `x-client-type: mobile` to get raw tokens in the JSON body instead, as this collection assumes) and WebAuthn passkey / TOTP 2FA / Google Sign-In / Sign in with Apple as alternate or additional login factors — see the Authentication folder for the full set.

**Roles.** `Role` enum: `BUYER`, `SELLER`, `RIDER`, `ADMIN`, `SUPPORT`, `ACCOUNTANT`. Every protected request's description states its allowed roles explicitly; requests with no role note (but auth required) accept any authenticated role.

**Rate limiting.** Sensitive endpoints (credential guessing, OTP requests, payments, payouts) are tiered and rate-limited server-side; hitting a limit returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header. See each folder's description for its specific limiter.

**Idempotency.** Financial mutation endpoints accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header to safely retry after network errors without double-processing.

Generated by inspecting `server/src/**` directly (route files, controllers, services, Prisma schema, middleware) — see `SwiftGoma-API-INVENTORY.md` alongside this collection for the full endpoint table this was built from.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness/readiness probes for the SwiftGoma API, used by uptime monitors, load balancers, and CI. `GET /health` is unauthenticated and safe to poll frequently. `GET /health/detailed` reports the connectivity of every downstream dependency (database, Cloudinary, SMTP, SMS, OneSignal, PawaPay, MbiyoPay) and is protected by a constant-time comparison against the `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN` secret, not user authentication — it is meant for internal ops tooling, not end users.

### Purpose
Returns a lightweight liveness/readiness signal for the API, including whether the database connection is currently up.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Response
`200 OK` with `{ "status": "ok" | "degraded", "timestamp": "<ISO date>" }` when the process is up. Returns HTTP `503` (with the same body, `status: "degraded"`) if the database is unreachable.

### Errors
- `503` — database connection check failed.

request.description:
### Purpose
Returns the connectivity status of every external dependency the API relies on: PostgreSQL, Cloudinary, SMTP mailer, SMS provider, OneSignal push, PawaPay, and MbiyoPay. Results are cached for 10 seconds server-side.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Headers
- `x-health-token` (required) — must exactly match the server's `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN` env var. Compared with a timing-safe hash comparison, not authentication middleware.

### Business Rules
- If `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN` is not configured on the server, or the header is missing/incorrect, the endpoint returns a generic `404 { "error": "not_found" }` instead of `401/403` — this deliberately hides the endpoint's existence from unauthenticated scanners.

### Response
`200 OK` (or `503` if any dependency is unhealthy) with `{ "healthy": boolean, "db": {...}, "cloudinary": {...}, "mailer": {...}, "sms": {...}, "oneSignal": {...}, "pawapay": {...}, "mbiyopay": {...} }`.

### Errors
- `404` — token missing/incorrect, or `HEALTH_CHECK_TOKEN` unset on the server (endpoint behaves as if it does not exist).

item.name: Authentication
item.description: Account creation and authentication for SwiftGoma. Supports email/password login, passwordless email-OTP login, Google Sign-In, WebAuthn passkeys, and optional TOTP-based two-factor authentication with backup codes. On successful login the web flow (default, no `x-client-type` header) receives the access token in an httpOnly `swg_access_token` cookie and the refresh token in an httpOnly `swg_refresh_token` cookie (scoped to `/api/v1/auth`); a request sent with header `x-client-type: mobile` instead receives `accessToken`/`refreshToken` directly in the JSON body, for native apps that cannot use cookies. Access tokens are short-lived JWTs (`role`, `sessionId` claims); refresh tokens are long-lived and are hashed (SHA-256) before being stored against a `Session` row, so refreshing also rotates the stored hash and updates `lastUsedAt`. Endpoints are tiered by brute-force sensitivity: account/social-login endpoints use `accountLimiter`, OTP-request endpoints (email-enumeration risk) use `otpRequestLimiter`, and credential-guessing endpoints (login, OTP verification, password reset, TOTP checks) use the tighter `credentialGuessLimiter`, which also feeds an IP auto-block after repeated violations. Most endpoints intentionally return a generic message regardless of whether the email exists, to avoid account enumeration.

request.description:
### Purpose
Registers a new SwiftGoma account with name + email, and emails a 6-digit verification OTP to confirm the address. If the email already exists but is unverified, the account is reused and a fresh OTP is issued (no duplicate account created).

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `name` (string, required) — 2 to 100 characters after trimming.
- `email` (string, required) — must match a basic email pattern; normalized to lowercase.
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`) — `"en"` or `"fr"`, used for the verification email copy.
- `role` (string, optional) — self-assignable role; one of `BUYER`, `SELLER`, `RIDER`. Defaults to `BUYER` if omitted. `ADMIN`, `SUPPORT`, `ACCOUNTANT` cannot be self-assigned.

### Validation
- Name must be 2-100 chars.
- Email must be a syntactically valid address.
- `role`, if provided, must be one of the self-assignable roles or a `422 ROLE_NOT_SELF_ASSIGNABLE` error is thrown.

### Business Rules
- If a verified account already exists for this email, a `409 CONFLICT` is returned.
- No password is set at this step — the account has no password until `POST /auth/password/create` is called later (or the user simply keeps using email-OTP / Google / passkey login).

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is the sanitized user object (no password/OTP fields), including `hasPassword: false` and `isEmailVerified: false`.

### Errors
- `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` — one or more fields failed validation.
- `409 CONFLICT` — the operation conflicts with the resource's current state (e.g. invalid status transition, duplicate resource, subscription/plan limit reached).
- `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` / `IP_BLOCKED` — rate limit exceeded for this endpoint; `Retry-After` header indicates the wait time.

### Purpose
Confirms an account's primary email using the 6-digit OTP sent by Create Account / Resend Verification.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, required).
- `code` (string, required) — the 6-digit OTP.

### Validation
- Email format validated.
- Code compared with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (constant-time).

### Business Rules
- OTP expires after 10 minutes (`OTP_EXPIRED`).
- Already-verified emails return `409 CONFLICT`.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is the sanitized user with `isEmailVerified: true`.

### Errors
- `404 NOT_FOUND` — no account for this email.
- `409 CONFLICT` — already verified.
- `422 OTP_EXPIRED` / `422 OTP_INVALID`.

### Purpose
Creates a new account from a verified Google ID token (Google Sign-In). Since Google already verifies the email, the account and its session are created in one step — no OTP round-trip.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `idToken` (string, required) — the Google Sign-In ID token, verified server-side against `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` via `google-auth-library`.
- `role` (string, optional) — self-assignable role (`BUYER`, `SELLER`, `RIDER`); defaults to `BUYER`.
- `deviceName` (string, optional) — friendly label stored on the created session.
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- If a user is already linked to this Google account, `409 CONFLICT`.
- If the email is already registered (password/OTP account) but not linked to Google, `409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` — the user must log in normally and link Google from account settings instead.
- Web clients receive `accessToken`/`refreshToken` as httpOnly cookies; sending header `x-client-type: mobile` returns them in the JSON body instead.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is `{ user }` (web) or `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` (mobile).

### Errors
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED` — missing, invalid, or expired access token.
- `409 CONFLICT` — the operation conflicts with the resource's current state (e.g. invalid status transition, duplicate resource, subscription/plan limit reached).
- `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` / `IP_BLOCKED` — rate limit exceeded for this endpoint; `Retry-After` header indicates the wait time.
- `409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED`.

### Purpose
Creates a new account from a verified Apple identity token (Sign in with Apple). Apple provides the user's full name only on the very first authorization (as a separate field on the client, never inside the token itself) — pass it as `name` on that first request; the server falls back to the local part of the email if omitted.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `idToken` (string, required) — the Sign in with Apple identity token, verified server-side against Apple's public JWKS (`https://appleid.apple.com/auth/keys`).
- `name` (string, optional) — full name; only meaningful on the very first authorization.
- `role` (string, optional) — self-assignable role (`BUYER`, `SELLER`, `RIDER`); defaults to `BUYER`.
- `deviceName` (string, optional) — friendly label stored on the created session.
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- If Apple does not return an email for this identity, `401 UNAUTHORIZED`.
- If a user is already linked to this Apple account, `409 CONFLICT`.
- If the email is already registered (password/OTP account) but not linked to Apple, `409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` — the user must log in normally and link Apple from account settings instead.
- Web clients receive `accessToken`/`refreshToken` as httpOnly cookies; sending header `x-client-type: mobile` returns them in the JSON body instead.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is `{ user }` (web) or `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` (mobile).

### Errors
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED` — missing, invalid, or expired access token, or Apple did not provide an email.
- `409 CONFLICT` — the operation conflicts with the resource's current state (e.g. invalid status transition, duplicate resource, subscription/plan limit reached).
- `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` / `IP_BLOCKED` — rate limit exceeded for this endpoint; `Retry-After` header indicates the wait time.
- `409 EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED`.

### Purpose
Logs in an existing account previously linked to this Google identity.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `idToken` (string, required) — Google Sign-In ID token.
- `deviceName` (string, optional).
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- If no account is linked to this Google identity but the email is registered another way, `409 GOOGLE_NOT_LINKED`.
- If no account exists at all for this email, `404 NOT_FOUND`.
- If the account is blocked, `403 FORBIDDEN`.
- If the account has TOTP 2FA enabled, this returns `{ requiresTotp: true, pendingToken }` instead of tokens — complete the login via `POST /auth/login/totp`.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is either `{ requiresTotp: true, pendingToken }` or `{ user }` (web, cookies set) / `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` (mobile).

### Errors
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED` — missing, invalid, or expired access token.
- `403 FORBIDDEN` — authenticated but role is not allowed, or an ownership check failed.
- `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` / `IP_BLOCKED` — rate limit exceeded for this endpoint; `Retry-After` header indicates the wait time.
- `404 NOT_FOUND` — no account for this Google identity.
- `409 GOOGLE_NOT_LINKED`.

### Purpose
Sends a 6-digit passwordless login code to the given email (email-OTP login flow), independent of any password.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, required).
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- Always returns the same generic message whether or not the account exists, is blocked, is deleted, or is unverified — this endpoint never confirms account existence (anti-enumeration).
- A resend cooldown of 30 seconds applies while a code is still active; requesting again inside the cooldown throws `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` with the remaining seconds in the message.
- The OTP is valid for 10 minutes.

### Response
`200 OK` with a generic `{ "message": "..." }` regardless of outcome.

### Errors
- `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` — one or more fields failed validation.
- `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` / `IP_BLOCKED` — rate limit exceeded for this endpoint; `Retry-After` header indicates the wait time.

### Purpose
Generates a WebAuthn authentication challenge for passkey login. Omit `email` for a usernameless (discoverable-credential) flow; provide it to scope the challenge to that account's registered passkeys.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, optional) — when provided, must be a valid email with at least one registered passkey, or `404 NOT_FOUND` is returned.

### Business Rules
- Requires Redis (`cache.isAvailable()`); if the cache layer is down, returns `503 WEBAUTHN_UNAVAILABLE`.
- The challenge is cached server-side for up to 60 seconds and must be echoed back (signed by the authenticator) to `POST /auth/passkey/login/verify`.

### Response
`200 OK` with WebAuthn `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions`, plus `challengeId` when the usernameless flow is used.

### Errors
- `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` — one or more fields failed validation.
- `404 NOT_FOUND` — the referenced resource does not exist (or does not belong to the caller).
- `403 FORBIDDEN` — authenticated but role is not allowed, or an ownership check failed.
- `503 WEBAUTHN_UNAVAILABLE`.

### Purpose
Sends a password-reset OTP to the given email, if an active account exists.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, required).
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- Always returns the same generic response regardless of whether the account exists/is blocked/deleted (anti-enumeration).
- A 30-second resend cooldown applies while a reset code is still active.
- The reset code is valid for 15 minutes.

### Response
`200 OK` with a generic `{ "message": "..." }`.

### Errors
- `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` — one or more fields failed validation.
- `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` / `IP_BLOCKED` — rate limit exceeded for this endpoint; `Retry-After` header indicates the wait time.

### Purpose
Completes passwordless login by exchanging a valid email-OTP for a session (access + refresh tokens).

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, required).
- `code` (string, required) — the 6-digit OTP from `POST /auth/login/request-otp`.
- `deviceName` (string, optional) — label stored on the created session.

### Business Rules
- Blocked accounts (`403`), soft-deleted accounts outside the recovery grace period (`404`), or within it (`403 ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING`) cannot log in.
- A successful login creates a new `Session` row, issues access/refresh tokens, and sends a "new login detected" security notification/email.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is `{ user }` (web, cookies set) or `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` (mobile).

### Errors
- `404 NOT_FOUND` — no account for this email.
- `403 FORBIDDEN` — account blocked.
- `403 ACCOUNT_DELETION_PENDING` — account soft-deleted but recoverable.
- `422 OTP_EXPIRED` / `422 OTP_INVALID`.
- `429` — see module notes on `credentialGuessLimiter`.

### Purpose
Logs in using email + password.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, required).
- `password` (string, required).
- `deviceName` (string, optional).
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- Returns the same generic `"Email ou mot de passe incorrect."` message for both a non-existent account and a wrong password (anti-enumeration).
- Email must be verified (`403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`) and the account must have a password set (`409 NO_PASSWORD_SET` if it was created via Google/OTP only).
- If TOTP 2FA is enabled, returns `{ requiresTotp: true, pendingToken }` instead of tokens; finish with `POST /auth/login/totp`.
- Password comparison uses bcrypt (`bcryptjs`, 12 salt rounds).

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is `{ requiresTotp: true, pendingToken }`, or `{ user }` (web) / `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` (mobile).

### Errors
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED` — unknown email or wrong password.
- `403 FORBIDDEN` — account blocked.
- `403 EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`.
- `409 NO_PASSWORD_SET`.
- `429` — credential-guess rate limit.

request.description:
### Purpose
Completes a login that returned `requiresTotp: true` (from password, Google, or passkey login) by verifying a TOTP code or a one-time backup code.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `pendingToken` (string, required) — short-lived (5 min) JWT returned by the first-factor login step.
- `code` (string, required) — 6-digit authenticator code, or an unused backup code.
- `deviceName` (string, optional).
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- TOTP codes are validated with a ±1 step (30s) window and each accepted time-step can only be used once (Redis-backed replay guard); if Redis is unavailable, verification fails closed.
- Backup codes are single-use and are consumed (marked `isUsed`) on successful match.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is `{ user }` (web) or `{ user, accessToken, refreshToken }` (mobile).

### Errors
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED` — expired/invalid `pendingToken`.
- `403 FORBIDDEN` — account blocked.
- `409 CONFLICT` — 2FA not enabled for this account.
- `422 TOTP_INVALID`.

request.description:
### Purpose
Verifies a signed WebAuthn assertion against the challenge from `POST /auth/passkey/login/options` and logs the user in.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Request Body Fields
- `email` (string, optional) — required only for the email-scoped flow; omit when using `challengeId` (usernameless flow).
- `challengeId` (string, optional) — returned by the usernameless options call.
- `response` (object, required) — the browser's WebAuthn `AuthenticationResponseJSON`.
- `deviceName` (string, optional).
- `locale` (string, optional, default `"en"`).

### Business Rules
- The challenge must not have expired (60s TTL) — otherwise `422 WEBAUTHN_CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`.
- The passkey's stored counter is updated after a successful assertion (clone-detection).
- If TOTP 2FA is also enabled on the account, returns `{ requiresTotp: true, pendingToken }` instead of tokens.

item.description: Seller onboarding: the seller business profile (separate from the user account — one `SellerProfile` per `SELLER` user) and its KYC (Know Your Customer) verification workflow. ### Purpose
Public product catalog listing with filtering, search, and sorting — powers the storefront browse/search pages.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Query Parameters
- `page`, `limit` (max 100).
- `categoryId`, `subcategoryId`, `shopId` — exact-match filters.
- `minPrice`, `maxPrice` — filtered against each product's cheapest variant.
- `currency` — `USD` or `CDF`.
- `search` — matches name/description/brand (case-insensitive).
- `inStockOnly` — `"true"` to exclude out-of-stock products.
- `city` — the seller's registered city.
- `sortBy` — `recent` (default, newest first), `popular` (by `popularityScore`), `priceAsc`, `priceDesc`.

### Business Rules
- Only returns `PUBLISHED` products belonging to `PUBLISHED`, non-deleted shops.
- Results are cached server-side for 2 minutes per unique filter combination.

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type. `data` is `{ products: [...], pagination: { page, limit, total, totalPages } }`. Each product includes its first image, cheapest variant, subcategory+category, and shop summary.

### Purpose
Creates a new product (in `DRAFT` status) under one of the seller's shops.

### Authentication
Required. Send `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` (or the `swg_access_token` cookie set by the web login flow).

### Authorization
Allowed roles:
- SELLER

### Files (multipart/form-data)
- `images` (files, optional, up to 10) — JPEG/PNG/WEBP, 5MB each; real content sniffed from magic bytes.

### Request Body Fields
- `shopId` (string, required) — must be owned by the caller.
- `subcategoryId` (string, required).
- `name` (string, required) — 2-100 characters.
- `description` (string, required) — 20-1000 characters.
- `brand` (string, optional).
- `unit` (string, optional, default `"piece"`) — one of `piece`, `kg`, `liter`, `pack`.
- `weightGrams` (number, required) — 1 to 500000.
- `expiresAt` (ISO date string, conditionally required) — required when the subcategory's category slug is `alimentation-boissons` (food/beverages).
- `currency` (string, required) — `USD` or `CDF`.
- `variants` (JSON array, required, min 1 item) — each item: `{ name?, attributes?, sku?, price (required), stock (required), isDefault? }`.

### Validation
- Price per variant must be within `PRICE_MIN`/`PRICE_MAX` for the chosen currency (USD: 0.10–5000; CDF: 100–15,000,000).
- Stock per variant must be 0–1,000,000.
- At least one variant is required; more than one sets `hasVariants: true`.

### Business Rules
- The shop must belong to the caller's seller profile (`404` otherwise).
- Requires an `ACTIVE` subscription (`409 CONFLICT` if none).
- The shop's current product count must be under the plan's `maxProducts` (`409 CONFLICT` otherwise).
- Photo count must be within the plan's `maxPhotosPerProduct` (`409 CONFLICT` otherwise).

### Response
All responses use the shape `{ "success": true, "data": <payload> }` on success. Errors use `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details", "requestId" } }` with the HTTP status code matching the error type.

### Errors
- `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` — one or more fields failed validation.
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED` — missing, invalid, or expired access token.
- `403 FORBIDDEN` — authenticated but role is not allowed, or an ownership check failed.
- `404 NOT_FOUND` — the referenced resource does not exist (or does not belong to the caller).
- `409 CONFLICT` — the operation conflicts with the resource's current state (e.g. invalid status transition, duplicate resource, subscription/plan limit reached).

item.name: Orders
item.description: The full order lifecycle: buyer checkout, seller fulfillment (accept/reject/prepare/handoff), rider delivery (pickup/en route/delivered/failed), buyer receipt confirmation, cancellation, QR-code handoff verification, and per-order buyer↔rider chat. Checkout (`POST /orders/checkout`) converts the buyer's per-shop cart into an `Order`; for `ONLINE_PAYMENT` it also creates an `OrderPayment` and kicks off a PawaPay deposit, leaving the order `AWAITING_PAYMENT` until the deposit callback confirms it. For `CASH_ON_DELIVERY` the order goes straight to `PENDING_SELLER_REVIEW` and the cart is cleared immediately. Status transitions are role-gated: sellers drive `accept → preparing → ready → (rider assigned/pickup)`; riders drive `picked-up → on-the-way → delivered/failed`; either buyer or seller can cancel depending on the current status. QR codes (`qrToken`) let a rider scan-verify a pickup or a buyer scan-verify delivery in person. `POST /orders/checkout` and financial mutations are rate-limited (`paymentLimiter`) and protected by `idempotencyGuard` (send an `Idempotency-Key` header, or retries are deduped automatically by request body hash) to make retries after a network blip safe.

- `shopId` (string, required).

item.description: Internal admin/finance API for PawaPay mobile-money deposits (collections), payouts (disbursements), and refunds. This is NOT a buyer-facing payment API — buyers pay via `POST /orders/checkout` and sellers subscribe via `POST /subscriptions`, both of which call PawaPay internally; this folder is for admin-initiated payouts/refunds and status inspection. Payouts and refunds are OTP-gated two-step flows (`request-approval` → `confirm`, mirroring Orders/Expenses/MbiyoPay) to prevent a compromised admin session alone from moving money; direct refund initiation is deliberately disabled server-side (`postInitiateRefund` always returns a validation error telling the caller to use the OTP flow). Valid `provider`/`country`/`currency` combinations are NOT a fixed enum in this codebase — they must match what `GET /pawapay/active-configuration` currently reports for PawaPay's supported corridors, since that endpoint mirrors PawaPay's own live configuration.

item.name: Payments — PawaPay Callbacks (Webhooks)
item.description: Inbound webhook endpoints called by PawaPay itself to report deposit/payout outcomes — never called by SwiftGoma clients. Mounted at `/api/v1/pawapay/callbacks`, outside normal user authentication. Authenticity is verified via PawaPay's request-signing scheme (`PAWAPAY_SIGNING_ENABLED`): the server reconstructs the full callback URL and verifies an inbound signature header against it. If signing is disabled, the server accepts callbacks unverified in non-production, but refuses to start accepting them at all in production (fails closed). Deposit callbacks route by `metadata.type` (e.g. `SUBSCRIPTION`) to the correct confirmation logic; `WALLET_TOPUP` deposit handling is a known stub (not yet implemented — logged and ignored). Always returns HTTP `200 { received: true }` even on internal processing errors, per PawaPay's expected webhook contract (so PawaPay doesn't endlessly retry a callback SwiftGoma already logged), except for a genuine signature failure which returns `401`.

header.description: PawaPay's request signature. Verified server-side; required in production.

item.description: Inbound webhook called by MbiyoPay to report cash-in/cash-out outcomes. Mounted at `/api/v1/mbiyopay/callbacks`, outside user authentication. Authenticity is verified via an HMAC `signature` header checked against the raw request body (`verifyWebhookSignature`); an invalid signature returns `401` before any processing happens. Routes `cashin` events to order-payment confirmation/failure and `cashout` events to either order-refund or seller-payout confirmation/failure, distinguishing the two by whether `order_id` starts with `SWG-REFUND-`. Always acknowledges with `200 { received: true }` even on internal processing errors, matching typical webhook-retry-avoidance conventions.

### Purpose
MbiyoPay calls this to report the outcome of a cash-in (customer payment) or cash-out (payout/refund) transaction.

### Authentication
Not required. Public endpoint.

### Headers
- `signature` (required) — HMAC over the raw body; requests with an invalid signature are rejected before any processing.

### Request Body Fields
- Body shape is defined by MbiyoPay, not SwiftGoma: `transaction_id`, `order_id`, `status` (`successful` | `failed` | `cancelled`), `type` (`cashin` | `cashout`).

### Business Rules
- `type: "cashin"` + `successful` — confirms the matching order's payment; `failed` — fails it.
- `type: "cashout"` — if `order_id` starts with `SWG-REFUND-`, treated as an order refund payout; otherwise treated as a seller wallet payout. `successful`/`failed`/`cancelled` route accordingly.

### Response
`200 OK` with `{ received: true }` (or `{ received: true, error: "internal_processing_error" }` on internal failure — still 200 by design).

### Errors
- `401 { received: false, error: "invalid_signature" }` — signature verification failed.

### Purpose
Removes a product from the current user's favorites.

### Authentication
Required. Send `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` (or the `swg_access_token` cookie set by the web login flow).

### Authorization
Any authenticated role may call this endpoint (no role restriction beyond authentication).

### Path Parameters
- `productId` (string, required).
